summary: Develop covers how to build, customize, publish and maintain Business Central apps and extensions. It answers questions about getting started as a partner, per-tenant customization, localization, marketplace submission and validation, embed apps, app lifecycle, and Microsoft versus partner responsibilities online.
overview:
The Develop section is for partners and developers who build on Business Central. It covers two paths: customizing a tenant (Designer for UI changes, AL extensions in Visual Studio Code for deeper changes, tested in sandbox environments first) and building apps to sell on the Microsoft commercial marketplace. It also has pages on localization apps and on the components and ecosystem integration options available to apps, such as APIs, Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps and Outlook add-in.

For publishers, the pages follow the app's life. "The SMB opportunity for app publishers" explains the market and app types (Connect and Add-on). "Get started building apps" walks through partner registration, publisher setup, unique object range and submission via Partner Center. "Add your App to Marketplace" covers marketing and technical validation. After release, the lifecycle, maintenance and discontinuation pages describe updates, breaking changes and removal. The Microsoft responsibilities page clarifies what Microsoft runs online and what partners maintain.

Two subtopics go deeper: Marketplace validation (technical checklist, marketing rules, landing pages and videos) and Embed apps (partner-branded solutions built on the platform). Start with "Get started building apps" for publishing, or "Customizing Tenants" for in-tenant changes.
key_points: Customizing tenants uses the in-client Designer for UI changes and AL extensions (page and table extensions, business logic) in Visual Studio Code, tested in sandbox or Docker before production.

Getting started as a publisher involves Partner Center registration, PartnerSource Business Center access, a unique object range, a developer license file, prefix or suffix registration, and technical validation.
Marketplace submission requires both marketing and technical validation, with special handling for embed apps.
Apps can integrate through a Dynamics 365 API endpoint, Outlook Add-in, Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps and Azure Machine Learning.
Localization apps address local regulatory requirements, national standards and market needs, using features like RapidStart data packages, translations and setup guides.

Maintaining Marketplace apps and per-tenant extensions means keeping up with major and minor releases, using preview versions, the AppSourceCop analyzer and automated validation to detect incompatibility.
Microsoft handles infrastructure, storage, high availability, disaster recovery, platform security, diagnostics and patching online. Partners maintain their own apps and extensions.
Discontinuing a Marketplace app involves stopping distribution, updating the listing (such as the Contact Me type), notifying customers and handling uninstallation.
